authority_boundary: Graph edge types are a reviewed, closed, versioned vocabulary. Generated graph edges are candidate evidence unless a local review process promotes a downstream decision.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: generated graph edge or MCP graph response
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Approval is a human or reviewed-policy gate, never generated graph evidence.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use review_status plus an explicit approval record pointer outside generated graph content.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: generated graph edge or MCP graph response
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Verification requires a reviewed validation artifact and cannot be inferred from graph structure.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use validated_by only for declared validation artifacts and keep review_status candidate until reviewed.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: generated graph edge or MCP graph response
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Trust tiers are reviewed source-policy facts, not generated graph outcomes.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Point to a reviewed trusted-source registry row when one exists.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: generated graph edge or MCP graph response
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Production readiness is a release and validation decision, not a graph relationship.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use validation pointers and human release gates outside generated graph content.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: generated graph edge or MCP graph response
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Comparative value claims require explicit evaluation methodology and review.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use candidate comparison evidence without ranking or recommendation language.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: generated graph edge or MCP graph response
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Recommendation is a decision surface and can create false authority.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use candidate route or candidate connection wording with authority_boundary.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: generated graph edge or MCP graph response
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Canon belongs to reviewed source-of-truth registries, not generated graphs.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use reviewed registry rows or source-of-truth pointers.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: generated graph edge or MCP graph response
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Authorization requires explicit policy and human gate evidence.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use approval IDs in audit or enrollment records outside generated graph content.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: generated inference without a declared dependency field
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Dependency order can affect rollout and must come from a declared registry field.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use declared.depends_on only; generated proximity can be similar_to, complements, co_used_with, or another candidate edge.

forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Replacement can retire or redirect assets and requires reviewed lineage.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use supersedes only for declared lineage evidence with review_status candidate until reviewed.

forbidden_edge_claims.blocked_when: bare generated graph edge without explicit causal methodology and review
forbidden_edge_claims.reason: Causal language overstates candidate graph evidence.
forbidden_edge_claims.replacement: Use evidence_for, gap_evidence_for, or another candidate non-causal relationship.

edge_types.semantics: A canonical lesson record names the repository where the lesson was learned.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Lessons can be routed to the wrong repo history.

edge_types.semantics: A lesson evidence pointer names a registered DAD offering.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Asset feedback and upgrade targeting can attach to the wrong offering.

edge_types.semantics: A lesson reusable-pattern value matches a reviewed pattern id or label.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Pattern-gap curation can be polluted by accidental prose matches.

edge_types.semantics: A repo usage ledger row says the repo is using an offering.
evidence_required: repo asset usage ledger row with status using
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Upgrade mail can target repos that are not using the asset.

edge_types.semantics: A repo usage ledger row says the repo is watching an offering for possible future use.
evidence_required: repo asset usage ledger row with status watching
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Future-use recommendations can spam repos with irrelevant upgrades.

edge_types.semantics: A declared lineage record says one mail packet, offering, or version replaces another.
evidence_required: declared supersedes field or lineage record
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Repos can retire or ignore the wrong asset version.

edge_types.semantics: A reviewed asset, skill, or offering names the intake or research record it was promoted from.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Research provenance can be lost or fabricated.

edge_types.semantics: A mail packet or lesson explicitly marks itself as a sighting of a reviewed pattern.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Pattern mining gets inflated by vague similarities.

edge_types.semantics: A reviewed offering or harness declares an eval case, test artifact, or validation command as supporting evidence.
evidence_required: declared validation artifact path or id
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: DAD can overstate promotion evidence.

edge_types.semantics: A registry row explicitly declares an asset dependency.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Update ordering and affected-repo analysis can become wrong.

edge_types.direction: asset -> asset (symmetric pair stored once, lower id first)
edge_types.semantics: Two same-category assets are near-duplicate or variant candidates and must route through semantic-evolution review.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: DAD can collapse distinct assets or create duplicate systems.

edge_types.direction: asset -> asset (symmetric pair stored once, lower id first)
edge_types.semantics: Two assets cover adjacent, non-overlapping workflow stages for a shared task context.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: False complements pollute combination discovery and waste review time.

edge_types.direction: asset -> asset (symmetric pair stored once, lower id first)
edge_types.semantics: Usage traces show assets used together in one or more repo sessions.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: DAD can spam bundled recommendations based on accidental co-use.

edge_types.semantics: A failure, review finding, or lesson provides evidence for an unmet DAD need.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Research and build effort can be misdirected.

edge_types.semantics: An asset is a hypothesized member of a multi-asset workflow combination.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Workflow recommendations can bundle unrelated assets.

edge_types.semantics: An immutable execution attempt names the exact role-profile revision used for that invocation.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Attempt results can be attributed to the wrong reusable role contract.

edge_types.semantics: An execution-attempt record names the source repository in which the bounded task ran.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Cross-repository evidence diversity and applicability can be overstated.

edge_types.semantics: An execution-attempt record attributes a provider/model family claim with an explicit verification status.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Attempt performance can be falsely attributed to a model or provider.

edge_types.semantics: A rubric-pinned evaluation identifies the immutable execution attempt it reviews.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Ratings and improvement notes can be attached to the wrong run.

edge_types.semantics: A criterion result names a candidate capability assessed for one execution attempt.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: A role or model can appear capable based on unrelated or absent evidence.

edge_types.semantics: A portable export was deterministically assembled from one validated archived revision under an explicit review record.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: An export can be attributed to bytes or authority it did not derive from.

edge_types.semantics: An inert archived revision records bytes captured in an immutable observation of an explicitly allowlisted personal source.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: An archive can be attributed to the wrong observation or treated as a currently active source.

edge_types.semantics: A content-specific archive revision belongs to one stable personal skill identity.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Revision history and disappearance/reappearance lineage can attach to the wrong skill.

edge_types.semantics: A DAD-managed runtime-neutral adaptation explicitly cites a personal-skill source marker.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: A DAD adaptation can be mistaken for an exact copy or original source.

edge_types.semantics: A reviewed export names its intended target runtime without claiming proven compatibility or installation.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Future agents can over-trust an intended target as proven compatibility.

edge_types.semantics: A declared runtime owns discovery of an active personal source; this does not authorize another runtime or archive copy to load it.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Archive or checkout presence can be mistaken for active installation.

edge_types.direction: archived revision -> archived revision (symmetric pair stored once)
edge_types.semantics: Two per-skill revisions have the same canonical tree content hash; authority, identity, and preferred source remain separate.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Hash equality can be misused to collapse identities or transfer authority.

edge_types.direction: skill or component -> declared capability family
edge_types.semantics: A registered skill or component explicitly declares that it implements a bounded family or capability contract.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: A prompt or component can be mistaken for a complete or installed capability family.

edge_types.semantics: A declared object names the governance contract that constrains its behavior and authority.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: A family can appear governed by a contract that does not actually apply or can conceal a conflicting authority boundary.

edge_types.direction: family, policy, or overlay -> bounded target
edge_types.semantics: A reviewed or candidate scope declaration says an object may be relevant to a named repository, project, workflow, or domain target.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: A relevance edge can be misread as adoption, installation, competence, data access, or mutation authority.

edge_types.direction: object or dependency -> sentinel or monitor
edge_types.semantics: A declaration assigns a read-only observer to report evidence-backed freshness, integrity, or lifecycle signals for an object.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Monitoring presence can be mistaken for complete coverage or an observer can silently acquire repair authority.

edge_types.semantics: A fingerprinted health projection says a specific evidence, dependency, compatibility, authority, or validation change makes an object's current status stale or unknown.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Age or an unrelated change can incorrectly retire useful guidance or flood the human review queue.

edge_types.semantics: Evidence shows two candidate contracts, authorities, dependencies, or recommendations cannot both be applied in the declared context without a human decision.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: False conflicts can block compatible work, while missed context can turn a local disagreement into an incorrect universal prohibition.

edge_types.semantics: A reviewed semantic structure declares a bounded child without transferring governance authority.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Semantic containment can be confused with sovereignty or source authority.

edge_types.semantics: The inverse structural assertion of contains; it never changes project sovereignty.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: A child can be routed under the wrong plan or authority.

edge_types.semantics: A candidate entity narrows the capabilities or scope of another entity.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Distinct peers can be collapsed into an incorrect hierarchy.

edge_types.semantics: Two entities have related outcomes without supported identity or hierarchy equivalence.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Unrelated work can create noisy routing candidates.

edge_types.semantics: An immutable plan revision names the concept or capability it intends to advance.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Execution evidence can attach to the wrong durable concept.

edge_types.semantics: A reviewed workstream binding advances a named immutable plan revision.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Portfolio attention can be assigned to unrelated work.

edge_types.direction: knowledge or asset entity -> target entity
edge_types.semantics: A declared library or asset provides bounded evidence or implementation support.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Presence of a library can be mistaken for complete capability coverage.

edge_types.semantics: A declared lineage record continues work without claiming identity equivalence or completion.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Unrelated work can inherit stale scope or acceptance claims.

edge_types.semantics: A bounded scope, audience, or implementation difference creates a candidate variant relationship.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Variants can be silently treated as interchangeable.

edge_types.semantics: Strong retrieval similarity requires a human identity disposition and preserves both identities.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Similarity can erase distinct plans or transfer authority.

edge_types.semantics: An explicit human identity decision preserves the retired ID and redirects future exact lookup.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: False merges can hide unique work and corrupt lineage.

edge_types.semantics: An explicit human decision preserves an overloaded historical identity while creating distinct successors.
edge_types.danger_if_wrong: Historical evidence can be attributed to the wrong successor.
